subject: CareEdge — retention & deletion workflow alignment (backup purge + log exception)
messages:
From: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@caredge.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CareEdge retention request + backup purge timeline

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for taking this. Attached is a short workbook (CareEdge_Data_Retention_Request.xlsx) that maps our product features to retention expectations. Legal is asking us to confirm:

- the deletion workflow and expected wall-clock time from request → live erase;
- whether backups will be included in the same window or on a staggered purge;
- whether logs (audit, request traces) can be held under an exception and for how long.

We have a procurement milestone next week and need to align on a conservative operational timeline we can put in the DPA appendix. Can you share a proposed phased purge plan and any log-retention exception process?

Also copying our procurement lead Tim to coordinate timing.

Best,
Sarah Ellis
Head of Privacy & Compliance
CareEdge Inc.

Attachments: CareEdge_Data_Retention_Request.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@caredge.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CareEdge retention request + backup purge timeline

Sarah —

Appreciate the workbook. I reviewed the tables and drafted a proposal (attached) that separates the workflow into three phases to match your compliance milestones:

Phase 1 — User-facing deletion: asynchronous in-system erase and confirmation (0–72 hours typical; up to 7 days conservative for complex objects).
Phase 2 — Nearline backup purge: scheduled job that removes tombstoned snapshots from hot backups in a staged window (30–45 days after Phase 1), with an opt-in fast purge for high-priority records.
Phase 3 — Deep archival expiration: cold storage compaction and index eviction (90–180 days depending on account settings and any legal hold).

For logs: we can offer a log-retention exception workflow where CareEdge requests an exception (documented request + justification) — our standard approval path requires SOC 2 signoff from infra + product, and the operational guardrails enforce access redaction and MAM scoping. Typical exception approvals for audit traces are 180 days with review every 90 days.

I've attached a short PDF "redwood-proposed-timeline-v1.pdf" and a draft mutual-action plan to show the gating points. Can Kimberly confirm the feasibility of the 0–72 hour in-system erase target for the product artifacts listed?

Next steps I propose:
- Kimberly to confirm technical constraints and any subprocessor impact;
- Redwood to provide a subprocessor snapshot for the DPA addendum;
- CareEdge to confirm whether the procurement team requires a DocuSign amendment or an annex.

Thanks — I can hop on a 30 min sync if helpful.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-proposed-timeline-v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@caredge.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CareEdge retention request + backup purge timeline

Jordan / Sarah —

Quick technical callouts on the proposed phases:

1) In-system erase (Phase 1): achievable for primary records. If objects have cross-references (embeddings, search indexes, materialized views) we need a secondary pass to remove derived artifacts — that can add up to 72 hours on a conservative cadence. We can mark the record status as "erased" immediately for API responses while background sweep finishes.

2) Nearline backup purge (Phase 2): our backups are snapshot-based with a retention snapshot chain. A purge of a specific object requires a tombstone write + snapshot compaction. Operationally, scheduling compaction every 24–48 hours for impacted shards is fine, but full per-account fast-path purge requires an ops playbook (we can enable a prioritized purge for an additional ops-window fee).

3) Logs & exceptions: audit and request traces live in a write-once index for 60 days by default. We can entertain exceptions up to 180 days with the following constraints:
  - Exception request submitted to security@redwood.com and classified (business, legal, audit);
  - Access limited through time-bound SSO roles and recorded RDP session traces;
  - Subprocessor access: we need to enumerate any third parties that will see unredacted traces.

Neha — can you pull the current subprocessor snapshot and confirm whether any backup or logging subprocessors (cloud storage, logging SaaS) will need to be added to the DPA? I can draft the technical language for the annex once we have that list.

Kimberly Park
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@caredge.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Timothy Bauer <tim.bauer@procurecorp.com>, audit@caredge.ai
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 12:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CareEdge retention request + backup purge timeline

Thanks Kimberly — that clarifies a lot. A couple of follow-ups from our side: 

- Procurement wants explicit confirmation that backups containing customer data will be purged under the same governance (they'll accept a staggered window provided it's codified in the annex).
- Legal requires proof of encryption-at-rest and a list of subprocessors that handle backups or logs (we will need the subprocessor snapshot for our DPA).
- For the log-retention exception: can Redwood commit to a single-person request owner and automated expiry reminders before the 180 day mark? We try to avoid open-ended access.

We can accept the 0–72 hour in-system erase if the background sweeper approach is documented in the annex. Tim — procurement is leaning toward a DocuSign annex for the retention/timeline tables; will that work for your team?

I've attached a small zip with our audit template (CareEdge_Audit_Attachments.zip) to show the fields we will put into the annex.

Best,
Sarah

Attachments: CareEdge_Audit_Attachments.zip (zip)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CareEdge retention request + backup purge timeline

Sarah / Team —

Thanks — confirming next steps and commitments from Redwood: 

1) We will provide a subprocessor snapshot (export) by EOD Thursday (2026-06-25) showing any cloud storage or logging vendors that touch backups/logs.
2) The DPA annex will include the phased purge table (Phase 1: 0–72 hours; Phase 2: 30–45 days; Phase 3: 90–180 days) and will state that backups are covered by Phase 2 compaction with a documented fast-path purge option.
3) For log-retention exceptions we will implement: single-person owner ticket, automated 30/15/7 day expiry reminders, and mandatory quarterly review if the exception extends beyond 90 days. Exception maximum 180 days.
4) Proof of encryption-at-rest: we will provide the KMS/implementation note and a compliance excerpt for the annex.

Kimberly / Neha — please confirm the subprocessor export and a short sentence about the fast-path ops fee so we can include it in the mutual-action plan. I will upload the MAP to the shared folder and start a DocuSign envelope for the annex placeholder.

I'll share the Drive link when the MAP is uploaded: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDEF-Map-Shared

If that all looks good I'll schedule a 30-minute wrap-up call Thursday morning (tentative invite to follow).

—Jordan
